# lobsteR

`lobsteR` provides a tidy workflow for requesting, downloading, and
reading [LOBSTER](https://app.lobsterdata.com/) high-frequency order
book data directly from R. LOBSTER reconstructs full limit order books
from NASDAQ historical message data and delivers them as pairs of
message files and order book snapshot files. This package handles the
end-to-end pipeline — authentication, request submission, archive
retrieval, and file download — so you can focus on analysis. For
downstream high-frequency econometrics, see the
[`highfrequency`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=highfrequency)
package.

**Prerequisites:** an active account at
[lobsterdata.com](https://app.lobsterdata.com/) is required to request
and download data.

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("lobsteR")
```

Or the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/voigtstefan/lobsteR):

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("voigtstefan/lobsteR")
```

## Workflow

``` r

library(lobsteR)
```

### 1. Authenticate

Store your credentials in `.Renviron` (open it with
`usethis::edit_r_environ()`) to avoid hardcoding them in scripts:

    LOBSTER_USER=you@example.com
    LOBSTER_PWD=your-password

Then authenticate:

``` r

lobster_login <- account_login(
  login = Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_USER"),
  pwd   = Sys.getenv("LOBSTER_PWD")
)
```

### 2. Build a request

[`request_query()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/request_query.md)
expands a symbol and date range into one row per trading day,
automatically removing weekends and NYSE holidays. `level` sets the
number of order book price levels included in the snapshot files
(e.g. `10` returns the top 10 bid and ask levels).

``` r

library(lobsteR)

request_query(
  symbol     = "MSFT",
  start_date = "2023-01-02",
  end_date   = "2023-01-13",
  level      = 10
)
```

    #>    symbol start_date   end_date level
    #> 2    MSFT 2023-01-03 2023-01-03    10
    #> 3    MSFT 2023-01-04 2023-01-04    10
    #> 4    MSFT 2023-01-05 2023-01-05    10
    #> 5    MSFT 2023-01-06 2023-01-06    10
    #> 8    MSFT 2023-01-09 2023-01-09    10
    #> 9    MSFT 2023-01-10 2023-01-10    10
    #> 10   MSFT 2023-01-11 2023-01-11    10
    #> 11   MSFT 2023-01-12 2023-01-12    10
    #> 12   MSFT 2023-01-13 2023-01-13    10

For large date ranges, use `frequency = "1 month"` to submit one request
per month rather than one per day, which reduces load on the LOBSTER
server.

### 3. Submit the request

``` r

request_submit(
  account_login = lobster_login,
  request       = data_request
)
```

LOBSTER processes requests server-side. Depending on the volume of
messages, this can take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours.
You can safely close your R session while waiting — processing continues
on the LOBSTER servers.

### 4. Check the archive

Once processing is complete, the files appear in your account archive:

``` r

lobster_archive <- account_archive(account = lobster_login)
lobster_archive
```

The returned tibble has one row per available dataset with columns `id`,
`symbol`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `level`, `size`, and `download`.

### 5. Download

``` r

dir.create("data-lobster", showWarnings = FALSE)

data_download(
  requested_data = dplyr::filter(lobster_archive, symbol == "MSFT"),
  account_login  = lobster_login,
  path           = "data-lobster"
)
```

Downloaded `.7z` archives are extracted automatically. Pass
`unzip = FALSE` to keep the raw archives. Note that extraction runs in a
background process, so the function returns before the files are fully
written to disk — check the `path` directory before proceeding with
analysis.

### 6. Clean and aggregate

[`lobster_clean()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_clean.md)
reads one day’s message and order book files, keeps continuous trading
and returns one row per message with the book state after it: midquote,
spread, depth within given distances from the best price, and the sign
of each trade.
[`lobster_snapshots()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_snapshots.md)
aggregates this to a regular grid (default 5 seconds).
[`lobster_process()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_process.md)
does both, also straight from a downloaded `.7z` archive, without
unpacking it:

``` r

days <- lobster_archive_files("data-lobster/MSFT_2023-01-03_2023-01-13_10.7z")

snapshots <- lobster_process(
  archive  = "data-lobster/MSFT_2023-01-03_2023-01-13_10.7z",
  date     = "2023-01-03",
  freq     = 5,          # seconds
  depth_bp = c(0, 5)     # depth at the best price and within 5 bp of it
)

lobster_crosses(snapshots) # opening and closing crosses: price and volume
lobster_halts(snapshots)   # trading halts
lobster_log(snapshots)     # messages dropped and kept
```

Each snapshot is labelled by the end of its interval and holds the
midquote at that instant; time-weighted spread and depth; signed volume
(shares, net buyer-initiated), trading volume and midpoint volume (USD);
the number of messages and trades; and flags for halts and for depth
that may be cut short by the number of levels in the file. Time stamps
are in New York time.

The main choices:

- Continuous trading runs from the opening cross (or 09:30) to 16:00 or
  the closing cross. Set `trading_hours = c("09:30", "13:00")` on
  early-close days. The crosses are reported, never mixed into the
  snapshots.
- Hidden executions are signed against the midquote just before the
  trade. Those exactly at the midquote (midpoint orders) stay unsigned:
  they count in `trading_volume` and `midpoint_volume`, not in
  `signed_volume`.
- Depth is measured from the best price on each side. Depth within `bp`
  basis points needs about `bp / 10000 * price / tick + 1` levels; for
  SPY at USD 520 and 5 bp that is 27 levels. `depth5_truncated` shows
  when the file has too few.

The functions read the order book block by block and only as deep as
needed, so memory use does not grow with the number of levels: a
50-level SPY day (7.2 million messages, 8.7 GB of order book CSV) takes
about a minute and 4 GB of RAM on a Raspberry Pi 5, read straight from
the archive. A polars version with the same functions and output is in
[`python/lobster_clean.py`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/python/lobster_clean.py).

## System dependencies on Linux

The `archive` package used for `.7z` extraction requires system
libraries. On a Debian/Ubuntu system:

``` bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y gpgv gnupg libarchive13t64 liblz4-dev libacl1-dev libext2fs-dev nettle-dev
sudo apt-get install -y libarchive-dev
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`account_archive()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/account_archive.md)
  : Retrieve LOBSTER data archive information
- [`account_login()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/account_login.md)
  : Authenticate with LOBSTER account
- [`data_download()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/data_download.md)
  : Download requested archive files
- [`lobster_archive_files()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_archive_files.md)
  : List the message and order book files in a LOBSTER archive
- [`lobster_clean()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_clean.md)
  : Clean one day of LOBSTER data
- [`lobster_file_info()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_file_info.md)
  : Parse LOBSTER file and archive names
- [`lobster_crosses()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_metadata.md)
  [`lobster_halts()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_metadata.md)
  [`lobster_log()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_metadata.md)
  : Crosses, halts and the cleaning log of a LOBSTER day
- [`lobster_process()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_process.md)
  : Clean one LOBSTER day and aggregate it to snapshots
- [`lobster_snapshots()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/lobster_snapshots.md)
  : Aggregate cleaned LOBSTER messages to a regular time grid
- [`request_query()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/request_query.md)
  : Create a LOBSTER data request (one row per trading day)
- [`request_submit()`](https://voigtstefan.github.io/lobsteR/reference/request_submit.md)
  : Submit one or more requests to an authenticated LOBSTER account
